arxiv-1807-02081.creator: Luca Aceto \rsuper a,b, Ignacio Fábregas \rsuper c, Álvaro García-Pérez \rsuper c, Anna Ingólfsdóttir \rsuper b, Yolanda Ortega-Mallén \rsuper d
arxiv-1807-02081.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Luca Aceto \rsuper a,b, Ignacio Fábregas \rsuper c, Álvaro García-Pérez \rsuper c, Anna Ingólfsdóttir \rsuper b, Yolanda Ortega-Mallén \rsuper d. The nominal transition systems (NTSs) of Parrow et al. describe the operational semantics of nominal process calculi. We study NTSs in terms of the nominal residual transition systems (NRTSs) that we introduce. We provide rule formats for the specifications of NRTSs that ensure that the associated NRTS is an NTS and apply them to the operational specifications of the early and late pi-calculus.

arxiv-2410-18340.title: Thermal Chameleon: Task-Adaptive Tone-mapping for Radiometric Thermal-Infrared images
arxiv-2410-18340.creator: Dong-Guw Lee, Jeongyun Kim, Younggun Cho, Ayoung Kim
arxiv-2410-18340.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Dong-Guw Lee, Jeongyun Kim, Younggun Cho, Ayoung Kim. Thermal Infrared (TIR) imaging provides robust perception for navigating in challenging outdoor environments but faces issues with poor texture and low image contrast due to its 14/16-bit format. Conventional methods utilize various tone-mapping methods to enhance contrast and photometric consistency of TIR images, however, the choice of tone-mapping is largely dependent on knowing the task and temperature dependent priors to work well.

arxiv-2411-14855.title: Applications of fractional calculus in learned optimization
arxiv-2411-14855.creator: Teodor-Alexandru Szente, James Harrison, Mihai Zanfir, Cristian Sminchisescu
arxiv-2411-14855.description: Abstract Fractional gradient descent has been studied extensively, with a focus on its ability to extend traditional gradient descent methods by incorporating fractional-order derivatives. This approach allows for more flexibility in navigating complex optimization landscapes and offers advantages in certain types of problems, particularly those involving non-linearities and chaotic dynamics.

arxiv-2503-09668.title: Comment on: “2005 VL1 is not Venera-2”
arxiv-2503-09668.creator: Abraham Loeb
arxiv-2503-09668.description: Abstract I show that the small differences between the orbital parameters of the dark comet 2005 VL 1 and the Venera 2 spacecraft (reported in arXiv:2503.07972) are of the magnitude expected from gravitational deflection by a close encounter of Venera 2 with Venus. I Introduction Seligman et al.

arxiv-2507-04955.title: Expotion: Facial Expression and Motion Control for Multimodal Music Generation
arxiv-2507-04955.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by . We propose Expotion (Facial Exp ression and M otion Control for Multimodal Music Generation), a generative model leveraging multimodal visual controls—specifically, human facial expressions and upper-body motion—as well as text prompts to produce expressive and temporally accurate music. We adopt parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) on the pretrained text-to-music generation model, enabling fine-grained adaptation to the multimodal controls using a small dataset. To ensure precise synchronization between video and music, we introduce a temporal smoothing strategy to align multiple modalities.

arxiv-2512-05617.title: Toward a Theoretical Roadmap for Organic Memristive Materials
arxiv-2512-05617.creator: Salvador Cardona-Serra 1,∗
arxiv-2512-05617.description: Abstract Neuromorphic computing aspires to overcome the intrinsic inefficiencies of von Neumann architectures by co-locating memory and computation in physical devices that emulate biological neurons and synapses. Memristive materials stand at the core of this paradigm, enabling non-volatile, history-dependent electronic responses.

arxiv-2512-11872.title: WAM-Diff: A Masked Diffusion VLA Framework with MoE and Online Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Driving
arxiv-2512-11872.creator: Mingwang Xu 1∗ Jiahao Cui 1∗ Feipeng Cai 2∗ Hanlin Shang 1∗ Zhihao Zhu 1 Shan Luan 1 Yifang Xu 1 Neng Zhang 2 Yaoyi Li 2 Jia Cai 2 Siyu Zhu ✉ 1 {}^{1}\textsuperscript{{\char 0\relax}} 1 Fudan University 2 Yinwang Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd
arxiv-2512-11872.description: Abstract End-to-end autonomous driving systems based on vision-language-action (VLA) models integrate multimodal sensor inputs and language instructions to generate planning and control signals. While autoregressive large language models and continuous diffusion policies are prevalent, the potential of discrete masked diffusion for trajectory generation remains largely unexplored.

britannica-1911-eschscholtz-johann-fried.title: Eschscholtz, Johann Friedrich (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-eschscholtz-johann-fried.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-eschscholtz-johann-fried.description: Article 'Eschscholtz, Johann Friedrich' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 9), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. traveller and naturalist, was born in November 1793, at Dorpat, where he died in May 1831. He was naturalist and physician to Otto von Kotzebue’s exploring expedition during 1815–1818. On his return he was appointed extraordinary professor of anatomy (1819) and director of the zoological museum of the university at Dorpat (1822), and in 1823–1826 he accompanied Kotzebue on his second voyage of discovery.

pmc-11436131.title: Use of Botulinum Toxin in Upper-Limb Tremor: Systematic Review and Perspectives
pmc-11436131.creator: Damien Motavasseli, Cécile Delorme, Nicolas Bayle, Jean-Michel Gracies, Emmanuel Roze, Marjolaine Baude
pmc-11436131.description: Background: Tremor is the most common movement disorder, with significant functional and psychosocial consequences. Oral medications have been disappointing or limited by side effects. Surgical techniques are effective but associated with risks and adverse events. Botulinum toxin (BT) represents a promising avenue but there is still no double-blind evidence of efficacy on upper limb function.

pmc-11512479.title: Acetylomics reveals an extensive acetylation diversity within Pseudomonas aeruginosa
pmc-11512479.creator: Nand Broeckaert, Hannelore Longin, Hanne Hendrix, Jeroen De Smet, Mirita Franz-Wachtel, Boris Maček, Vera van Noort, Rob Lavigne
pmc-11512479.description: Bacteria employ a myriad of regulatory mechanisms to adapt to the continuously changing environments that they face. They can, for example, use post-translational modifications, such as Nε-lysine acetylation, to alter enzyme activity. Although a lot of progress has been made, the extent and role of lysine acetylation in many bacterial strains remains uncharted.

pmc-11689261.title: HOW DOES THE USE OF HIGH-COST TREATMENTS IMPACT UTILIZATION OF THE MEDICARE HOSPICE BENEFIT?
pmc-11689261.creator: Michael Plotzke, Thomas Christian
pmc-11689261.description: Medicare patients who may benefit from palliative chemotherapy, radiation, or blood transfusions for symptom management (hereafter called “high-cost treatments”) may face difficulties accessing those treatments while electing hospice. The Medicare hospice benefit allows these high-cost treatments, but the treatments’ cost may exceed hospice agencies’ Medicare payments, limiting hospices’ ability to cover high-cost treatments.

pmc-12444270.title: Animal models for study on rotator cuff healing
pmc-12444270.creator: Qi-Long Jiang
pmc-12444270.description: Rotator cuff tears are highly prevalent, and there is an urgent need to understand their healing mechanisms to improve treatment outcomes for patients. This editorial aims to summarize the roles and limitations of common animal models (including rodents, rabbits, sheep, dogs, and primates) and second-look arthroscopy in rotator cuff healing research. Different animal models offer distinct advantages and disadvantages.

pmc-12540570.title: Methods for Assessment of Sleep and Circadian Rhythms in Cardiovascular Research
pmc-12540570.creator: Rebecca Williams, Gabrielle Gloston, Katherine C Ward, Shubhi Jain, Kristen Hays, Annie Ensor, Samarth Patel, Neel Patel, Mackenzie Hogue, S Justin Thomas, Brittanny M Polanka
pmc-12540570.description: Sleep is recognized in Life’s Essential 8™ as an important behavioral factor for improving and maintaining cardiovascular health. While sleep duration is currently the focus in Life’s Essential 8™, sleep health is multidimensional and encompasses regularity, satisfaction, next-day alertness, timing, efficiency, and duration. In addition to sleep, circadian factors have also been implicated in cardiovascular health.

pmc-12548013.title: Fundamental Understanding of “Fresh” Lithium Nucleation and Growth in Sulfide‐Based Anode‐Free Solid‐State Batteries: Effects of Substrate, Current Density, and Li+ Supply
pmc-12548013.creator: Jiwei Wang, Yuzi Liu, Mengting Ye, Guanyi Wang, Cheng Xu, Hongli Zhu
pmc-12548013.description: Understanding the electrochemical extraction and deposition of lithium (Li) from cathode is crucial for advancing anode‐free solid‐state batteries (AFSSBs). Herein, cryo‐transmission electron microscopy (cryo‐TEM) and electrochemical studies are employed to investigate how current collector surface properties, current densities, and cathode loadings influence the morphology of fresh electrochemically deposited Li and the electrochemical performance in sulfide‐based AFSSBs.

pmc-13191652.title: When cellulitis isn’t cellulitis: A case of rapidly progressive cutaneous hemorrhagic bullae and purpura with mucosal involvement
pmc-13191652.creator: Lauren James, Phuong Daniels, Shelby Boock, Chelsea Schwartz, Ashley Rice
pmc-13191652.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). th non-healing lower extremity ulcerations. Two months earlier, he was hospitalized for volume overload that was complicated by the development of lower extremity wounds. Despite completing 3 courses of cephalexin for presumed cellulitis, the patient’s wounds persisted. In the emergency department, he was found to have fever, new-onset anemia, hematuria, patchy lung opacities, and enlarging lower extremity ulcerations, purpura, and hemorrhagic bullae. Over the next 48 hours, his cutaneous findings rapidly progressed to involve the trunk, upper extremities, and multiple mucosal sites.

pmc-13263825.title: Case report: durable response to osimertinib, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy combination in advanced non-small cell lung cancer with atypical metastasis
pmc-13263825.creator: Javier Arias-Romero, Isa Mambetsariev, Jeremy Fricke, Razmig Babikian, Pauline Kim, Shaira Therese Dingal, Trilokesh D. Kidambi, Evan Pisick, Leonidas Arvanitis, Yu Liang, Bihong T. Chen, Mustafa Raoof, Arya Amini, Ravi Salgia
pmc-13263825.description: BackgroundA 71-year-old female never-smoker, with a remote history of secondhand smoke and a medical history including hyperlipidemia, hypertension, fatty liver, and chronic thrombocytopenia. Additionally, her family history is significant for multiple first-degree relatives with malignancy, including a father with lung cancer.Case DescriptionAn initial abdominal ultrasound revealed multiple hepatic lesions concerning for metastatic disease.

pmc-13284116.title: Exploring Taphrina deformans, the Springtime Scourge of Peach
pmc-13284116.creator: Clotilde Nigon, Morgane Roth, Bénédicte Quilot
pmc-13284116.description: Peach leaf curl, caused by the fungal pathogen Taphrina deformans, is a recurrent disease in peach orchards during spring.Host Range Taphrina deformans infects mostly peach ( Prunus persica ) and less significantly other Prunus crops.Disease SymptomsCausing severe leaf deformation and massive defoliations, leaf curl can drastically reduce tree vigour and yield and, in severe cases, lead to tree death.

pmc-13348740.title: Evaluating the Significance of Coagulation Tests for the Prevention and Treatment of Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation: A Meta-Analysis
pmc-13348740.creator: Lili Chen, Yangyang Zhang, Qiqi Ni
pmc-13348740.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background:We aimed to assess the clinical significance of obstetric coagulation tests in the prevention and treatment of disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) and to analyze the characteristics of changes in key coagulation indicators during pregnancy and delivery.Methods:The system searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of science, Wanfang Data knowledge service platform, VIP and China Knowledge Network databases for relevant literature from inception to Aug 2024. Two researchers independently screened the literature, extracted the information and evaluated the risk of bias of the included studies.

pmc-13418249.creator: Johannes Raedler, Florian Gothe, Thomas Magg, Philipp Peters, Karen Helene Bronken Martinsen, Ursula Holzer, Ayca Kiykim, Ayse Kalyoncu Ucar, Roshini S Abraham, Hemalatha G Rangarajan, Adeeb NaserEddin, Polina Stepensky, Irina Zaidman, Ehud Even-Or, Joern-Sven Kuehl, Daniel Graefe, Venetia Bigley, Christo Tsilifis, Anders Fasth, Nizar Mahlaoui, Oliver Wegehaupt, Carsten Speckmann, Jean-Laurent Casanova, Christoph Klein, Bénédicte Neven, Vivien Béziat, Romain Lévy, Fabian Hauck

pmc-13539214.title: HPV Vaccine Uptake, Hesitancy and Information Sources Among Young Adults: A Cross‐Sectional Study of Korea and the US
pmc-13539214.creator: Soojung Jo, Dongjuan Xu, Hwanseok Song
pmc-13539214.description: Background and AimsDespite the high effectiveness of HPV vaccination, uptake among young adults remains suboptimal. Healthcare policies, vaccine hesitancy, and sources of vaccine information may contribute to differences in vaccination behaviors across countries. To examine cross‐national and sex‐specific differences in HPV vaccine uptake and hesitancy among undergraduates in the US and Korea, and investigate the role of information sources.

pmc-13651147.title: Nonlinear modeling of health checkup factors and future claims-based healthcare costs in Japan: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-13651147.creator: Haruto Nakamura, Kaisei Harada, Kohei Hirako, Toshitaka Sawamura, Kousuke Imamura, Masahiko Sagae, Hidetaka Nambo, Shigehiro Karashima
pmc-13651147.description: BackgroundPopulation health checkups support disease prevention and health management. Clarifying how routinely collected checkup factors relate to subsequent healthcare costs may inform population-level risk assessment and preventive planning. We aimed to characterize nonlinear and sex-specific associations between routine checkup factors and near-term claims-based healthcare costs in Japan and to explore whether composite metabolic indices provide additional information beyond routine measures.

uslaw-usc-t18-s3611.title: 18 U.S.C. § 3611 — Payment of a fine or restitution
uslaw-usc-t18-s3611.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t18-s3611.description: United States Code, Title 18 (Crimes And Criminal Procedure); Part II (Criminal Procedure); Chapter 229 (Postsentence Administration); Subchapter B (Fines). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. A person who is sentenced to pay a fine, assessment, or restitution, shall pay the fine, assessment, or restitution (including any interest or penalty), as specified by the Director of the Administrative Office of the United States.
